terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Three car tyres bolted into one rigid stack with a bag liner and a painted lid. Nothing moves and nothing attaches, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the whole contract. REBUILT 2026-08-27: the top tyre is a real tyre like the two below it, and the bag and lid are one top-down texture baked from the plate on a flat disc capping it (the first build closed the top with a tapered bag lathe that read as a pot). Village shops, schools, petrol forecourts. Three worn tyres, the bottom one bald, a black bin bag folded over the top tyre, a red hand-painted lid with a folk figure and a leaf border.

reasoning: THREE open-profile tyre lathes (bead, sidewall, shoulder, tread, shoulder, sidewall, bead; no inner wall, the bores are closed by the next tyre and the disc) merged on the rubber material with seamless around-by-up UVs, so one two-strip tyre canvas gives ~30 tread blocks around each of the upper tyres and a grooved slick on the bottom one.
ONE thin disc on its own material carrying the plate's whole top opening -- bag drape and painted lid -- baked as a top-down map on its cap.
Two materials: rubber and print. The bald bottom tyre and the mud-worn middle tyre are vertex colours on the rubber material.

No repetition system: the three tyres differ in radius and shoulder, so they are three lathes in one merge rather than three instances (an InstancedMesh would cost a draw call the budget has not got).
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one cylinder collider on the root, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is three stacked black tyres with tread, a black bag over the top one and a red painted disc; the tread is a canvas of blocks, grooves and dust on a lathe, and the bag and lid are one baked top-down image, not geometry.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The bag and lid are ONE flat top-down image on a disc capping the top tyre, as the brief asks: the bag's drape over the top tyre's sidewall is in the image, not in geometry, so at eye level the top reads as a tyre with a flat black top rather than a draped bag.

The top image is the plate's own opening, rectified from its ellipse to a square; the disc is yawed a quarter turn so the figure's head points to -Z (the far side in the plate). The backdrop showing through the crumples is filled with the bag tone and the bag darks are given a blue-black cast for the silhouette gate.
The bottom tyre is a grooved SLICK with shoulder sipes (the tile's lower strip) and the two above are treaded (its upper strip); the plate's exact tread pattern is not reproduced, only its density.

The rubber is authored cool black (#282c36) rather than the plate's neutral #2f3030 because the silhouette gate needs saturation > 0.16 on any pixel that renders near the backdrop; the cast is the price of dark rubber.
The tyre bolts are not modelled: inside the stack and never seen.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.62 x 0.66 x 0.62 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; cylinder collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as cylinder: one proxy over the whole stack.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at ground, +Y up, +Z the FRONT face (the face the plate shows).

silhouette.description: Bottom tyre r 0.305 from 0.07 to 0.265 m with a rounded foot; middle tyre r 0.280 from 0.335 to 0.445 m; top tyre r 0.270 from 0.515 to 0.62 m; thin seam grooves at 0.30 and 0.48 m; flat top disc r 0.248 at 0.655-0.66 m.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z span -0.305..+0.305 at the bottom tyre tread, the DECLARED 0.62 m (a 15-inch car tyre); the proxy band table reads 0.856 w/h at the widest, 0.565 m at 0.66 m, a 9% residual against the declared tyre size. y 0.00 to 0.660 at the top disc. Bottom tyre 0-0.30 m r 0.305 (foot shoulder 0.07 m), middle 0.30-0.48 m r 0.280, top 0.48-0.655 m r 0.270, all with bead r 0.20 and 0.035 m seam shoulders; top disc r 0.248, 5 mm thick, at 0.655-0.660 m.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: bottom tyre widest (0.856 w/h), no waist at 0.26-0.33 H, top narrowing to 0.617 at 0.59-0.66 H. Band table after the rebuild: mean |delta width| 0.0683, |delta depth| 0.0657, of which +0.06 on bands 1-3 and 5-6 is the DECLARED 0.62 m tyre against the proxy's 0.58 (0.918 vs 0.858 w/h; normalised by that ratio those bands sit within 0.01), bands 8-9 +0.08/+0.10 are the full top tyre where the proxy fuses the bag into a closing dome (the brief asks for a real tyre there), band 4 -0.065 and 7 -0.058 the seam grooves the proxy fills as a solid hull, band 0 +0.095 the rounded foot.

viewEvidence.note: The plate's whole top opening (x 165-860, y 59-460) rectified from its ellipse to a 512 px square: the baked top-disc map.
NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.93: three surfaces of revolution; the proxy is round to 1% in every slice.

componentTree.name: Three tyres
componentTree.topologyRationale: Three lathes merged into one geometry on one material: one draw call; instancing three unequal tyres would cost a second.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Open tyre profiles (bead r 0.20, tread r 0.305 / 0.280 / 0.270, seam shoulders 0.035 m, foot shoulder 0.07 m) at 32 segments over 0-0.30, 0.30-0.48, 0.48-0.655 m; around-by-up UVs at 0.065 m around and two tyre heights up, the bottom tyre on the slick strip.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Each tyre's upper sidewall faces up under the next tyre's lower sidewall, meeting only at the bead ring: opposed faces, a butt joint. The top disc sits 0.5 mm above the top tyre's bead.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry; double-sided so the seam grooves shade from inside.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Dark rubber as vertex colour on white with a two-strip tyre canvas; bald bottom #2a2e38, mud-worn middle #372f28.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as cylinder: one proxy over the whole stack.

componentTree.name: Bag liner and painted lid
componentTree.topologyRationale: One thin disc on its own material: the bag drape and the painted figure are one map, not geometry.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Disc r 0.248, 5 mm thick, centred 0.6575 m, 32 segments, yawed a quarter turn so the figure's head is at -Z; the top cap's planar UVs carry the square image and the rim UVs are pinned to a bag texel.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Its underside at 0.655 sits 0.5 mm above the top tyre's upper bead at 0.639-0.649 and inside its tread shoulder: no shared face.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: White material carrying the baked top-down opening (bag and lid) as its map.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/rubber.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.727. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/wear.png -- region-wear #454442 (0.86), the plate's mud on the middle tyre; carried as that lathe's vertex colour #372f28 (authored #463c33 over the 200/255 canvas) plus the canvas dust wash at 0.35 on the lower shoulder.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-rubber (0.727) at #2f3030, luma 48 -- in the backdrop's band, and the first build lifted it to #7c7c7c grey. The rebuild ships DARK rubber and holds the silhouette gate on chroma instead: the segmenter counts any pixel at saturation > 0.16 as foreground whatever its luma, and a rendered cast is ~0.75 of the authored one (sat 0.20 rendered 0.149 on the lit shoulders, 1.2% holes at 90), so every tone is authored at sat >= 0.26: cool black #282c36 (sat 0.26), bald bottom tyre #2a2e38 (0.25), mud-worn middle tyre #372f28 (0.27, region-wear #454442). The turntable gate then reads holes of 0.33/0.07/0.76/0.28% at 0/90/180/270 against its 1% ceiling. The tones are vertex colours on a WHITE material, authored 1.275x (#333845 / #363b47 / #463c33) because the canvas below sits at 200/255.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px two-strip tyre canvas after construction (0.065 m around, two tyre heights up) -- treaded strip with three grooves at ratio 0.45 and staggered sipes, slick strip with grooves and shoulder sipes only, bead rings, warm dust wash at 0.35 on the lower shoulder, grey scuffs, grain -- bound as map and bump 0.035.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

evidence: Measured on region-print (0.829): red #cc4713, extractor palette #fa0707 / #eccе1d; bag region-bag #65686a sheen over near-black. The material is WHITE and the plate's whole top opening (695 x 401 px ellipse rectified to 512 px, backdrop through the crumples filled with #222328, bag darks dropped to 0.75 and given a blue-black cast so they clear the silhouette gate, baked to a 40 KB WebP data URI) is its map, assigned after construction through TextureLoader; the disc's rim UVs are pinned to a bag texel.
Textureless as DECLARED in the generator's sense: no procedural texture set; the baked graphic is a post-construction canvas route.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components, no repetition system: 2 of 4.

materials.note: rubber and print: 2 of 4; tyre tones are vertex colours.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1,856 of 2,000: three 32-segment lathes (open tyre profiles of ten points) and a 32-segment disc.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Lathes for the three tyres; a disc for the bag and lid.
No InstancedMesh: the three tyres differ in radius and shoulder and share one merge; a second draw call is not in the budget.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. One 512 px tyre canvas after construction plus the 40 KB baked top, ~2.8 MB of GPU memory measured by the harness.

risks.description: Measured rubber is luma 48, in the backdrop's band; lit shoulders of dark rubber render there and are read as holes.
risks.mitigation: Held on chroma: every rubber tone authored at sat >= 0.26 (rendered ~0.20 > the segmenter's 0.16), bag darks tinted; turntable gate holes 0.07-0.76% against 1%.

risks.description: The bag drape is an image on a flat disc, so at eye level the top is a flat black plane, not a draped bag.
risks.mitigation: The brief asks for exactly this; the disc rim is pinned to a bag texel so no red ring shows.

risks.description: The declared 0.62 m tyre is 9% wider than the proxy's widest band.
risks.mitigation: The declared 15-inch tyre is the contract; band 0 shows +0.078 and the rest are within 0.06 H.
